brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand-level fabric string is 'X-Pac VX21 / LS21 / LS42 Liteskin, HDPE spines, closed-cell foam, EPDM grip panels'. This holds up across the whole catalogue, not just the printed colorways: the bright prints (Rad Splatter, Trout, B&W Checkerboard on the SnakPaks and RukSak) obviously show the print sitting on an X-Pac-weight ripstop face fabric, but the SOLID colors also confirm it - the swatch photo filed under FramePak (framepak-framepak-custom-made-to-measure-1.jpg, a flat-lay closeup of plain red fabric with no product in frame) shows the diagonal X-Pac diamond grid stitch clearly even in a solid color, and the same faint diagonal grid is visible on the black DropperPak V.2 body in the studio photo. So unlike Swift Industries (where the grid was only confirmed on one product), JPaks' fabric string is well evidenced across prints and solids alike.
brand_notes.assetMismatch: framepak-framepak-custom-made-to-measure-1.jpg is not a photo of a FramePak - it is a flat, out-of-focus closeup of plain red X-Pac swatch fabric with no bag, strap, or hardware visible. Kept only as fabric evidence (see brand_notes.fabric), not used for FramePak's geometry/dims - framepak-framepak-custom-made-to-measure-2.jpg (two triangular frame bags on a cutting table) was used for that instead.
brand_notes.gearBagsRequireHardware: The Refugi Harness (barroll slot) is explicitly a harness only - roll-top drybags are sold separately, so liters is 0 by definition and there is nothing to render as bag volume, only the foam mounting cradle. Flagged per-product below.

products.name: Standard SnakPak 9.5"
products.dims_raw: Only the product name publishes a figure: 'Standard SnakPak - 9.5"'. No width, height, or litre figure is published anywhere on the page.
products.dims_note: len=24.1cm (9.5in) is the one real, maker-published number - the bag's fixed nose-to-tail length, no unfurled/packed distinction applies since this is a rigid zippered shell, not a roll-top. hgt and wid are my estimate from the studio photos: a squat wedge roughly 10cm tall at the nose, narrowing in width toward the tail. Not a range, so the new min-height rule doesn't apply here.

geometry.notes: Squared-off wedge, flat top with a top-mounted zip, tapers narrower toward the tail for knee clearance. Nose end (wide, velcro tab visible) mounts toward the head tube/stem; tail (narrow point) toward the saddle.

closure.hardware: single top-mounted zip running the full length, plastic zipper pull

details.fabric: X-Pac ripstop with printed graphic face (Donut, Rad Splatter, Trout Print, Black Topo, B&W Checkerboard) or plain X-Pac in solid colors - see brand_notes.fabric

mount.notes: Straps directly beneath the top tube via velcro plus the underside daisy-chain grippers; sits centred on the tube (wid centred at z=0), rising straight up (+y) from the tube surface. Nose (wide end) faces the head tube/stem, tail (narrow end) faces the saddle.

products.name: LargeFarva SnakPak 15"
products.dims_raw: Only the product name publishes a figure: 'LargeFarva SnakPak - 15"'. No width, height, or litre figure is published.
products.dims_note: len=38.1cm (15in) is the real maker-published length. hgt and wid are my estimate, scaled up slightly from the Standard SnakPak's proportions since this is the largest bag in the same wedge family (9.5in/12in/12in EXT/15in run). No published range, so the min-height rule doesn't apply.

geometry.notes: Same squared wedge family as the Standard SnakPak, longer body, slightly deeper cross-section. Camo colorway photo shows the top zip runs the full length with a visible ridge/batten along the spine (matches the HDPE-spine construction in brand aesthetic notes).

closure.hardware: single top-mounted zip running the full length, pull tab with a small loop

details.fabric: X-Pac ripstop, printed (Rad Splatter shown) or solid/camo - see brand_notes.fabric
details.notes: Two adjustable internal velcro dividers per dims_raw source text (not visible externally).

mount.notes: Same mounting as the Standard SnakPak: velcro plus rubber-gripper daisy chain underneath, centred on the tube, nose toward the head tube.

products.name: DropperPak V.2
products.dims_raw: No dimensions and no litre figure anywhere on the JPaks page. Described only as adding length and clearance over V.1, a third rear compression strap, and an HDPE spine.
products.dims_note: No maker figures exist at all - not even a range to apply the min/unfurled rule to. All three axes are my estimate from the on-bike photos: len is the full nose-to-tail run with the roll extended (photo 1, black); wid is the widest point at the nose/harness end (photo 3, blue); hgt is my estimate of the ROLLED (minimum) height, following the spirit of the new rule even though no published range exists to source it from - see render.basis.

geometry.notes: Nose is a rigid harness/cradle held off the seatpost by the DropStop clamp (visible as a grey collar around the seatpost in photo 1); the roll-top drybag body tapers to a narrow rolled tail. Photo 3 (blue) shows a two-part construction: a black cradle at the nose with daisy loops, and a separate roll-top liner bag compressed by straps.

closure.hardware: side-release buckle at the tail tip; 3 compression straps (per dims_note source text) cinch the roll

details.reflective: reflective piping visible along the compression-strap edge in the black colorway
details.fabric: X-Pac, faint diagonal grid visible even in the solid black colorway - see brand_notes.fabric

mount.notes: DropStop clamp holds the whole bag off the seatpost/dropper stanchion so it clears the seal head when the post drops - this is a rigid standoff, not a strap cinched directly to the post. A separate strap set also loops up around the saddle rails per photo 1.

render.basis: No height figure is published at all (not even a range). Estimated from the on-bike blue-colorway photo (dropperpak-dropperpak-v-2-one-size-3.jpg), which shows the roll-top liner turned down twice against a nose width of roughly 15cm - the packed height reads noticeably shorter than the nose is wide.

products.name: RukSak V.2
products.dims_raw: No dimensions or litre figure published; sized around 'a water bottle or frosty beverage'. Sold individually (bagsPerListing: 1), not as a pair - the page states this explicitly.
products.dims_note: All axes are my estimate. The closed-cell foam liner gives the body a fixed cylindrical height; the drawcord collar above it gathers closed but is short and does not meaningfully change the overall rendered height, so I have not treated this as a variable-height/roll item. hgt reduced slightly from a first-pass 17cm to 15cm to better match the body:collar ratio visible in the studio photos.

geometry.notes: Closed-cell foam liner cylinder with a pleated expandable mesh panel wrapping roughly half the circumference on the outer/leading side (checkerboard and camo photos both show the mesh panel is wider than a third of the body), drain grommet visible in the base.

closure.hardware: single drawcord with a plastic cord-lock and loop pull, red or white cord depending on colorway

details.fabric: X-Pac printed face (Rad Splatter, Duck Camo, B&W Checkerboard shown) over a closed-cell foam liner - see brand_notes.fabric

mount.notes: Universal left or right of the stem per the maker's own description - hangs from a single side-mounted buckle strap around the bar, cylinder axis vertical. Sold and mounted individually (one bag, one side); len/wid are just the diameter so their axis mapping is arbitrary for the round cross-section.

products.name: FramePak (Custom)
products.dims_raw: Fully custom to the rider's frame triangle - no dimensions or litre figure published anywhere.
products.dims_note: Fully custom product, so there is no single correct answer; these are a mid-range estimate for a 56cm gravel front triangle. framepak-framepak-custom-made-to-measure-1.jpg (filed as this product's first image) is NOT a photo of this product - it is a plain fabric swatch closeup with no bag visible (see brand_notes.assetMismatch) and was not used as sizing evidence. Only image 2 (two bags on a cutting table) was used.

geometry.notes: Full-frame triangle bag: narrow/pointed at the head tube end, full depth along the seat tube/BB end. Photo shows two bags side by side, one with a narrower waist - JPaks builds these per-frame, so the exact taper varies by customer bike.

closure.hardware: single zip following the top edge (along the down tube/top tube line), orange pull tabs, orange contrast stitching

details.fabric: X-Pac in solid colors (RX30 Cayenne shown), diagonal grid confirmed on the swatch photo - see brand_notes.fabric

mount.notes: Fills the full front triangle: underside rides along the down tube, top edge runs under the top tube, nose loop anchors near the head tube. Straps or JPaks' own bolt-on mounting washers per the maker's mount description; bolt-on option not visible in these photos.

products.name: Refugi Harness
products.dims_raw: No dimensions published. This is a HARNESS, not a bag - roll-top drybags that clip into it are sold separately.
products.dims_note: liters is 0 by definition, not unmeasured - there is no bag volume here, only the foam mounting cradle. dims_cm is my estimate of the cradle panel itself, scaled from the on-bike photo against the visible brake lever/handlebar for reference. Image 1 shows a single foam mounting block in isolation (one of a pair), not the assembled harness - image 2 (on-bike, Chumba drop-bar gravel bike) is the better geometry reference and confirms fitment on a drop-bar frame.

geometry.notes: Flat shield-shaped foam cradle, wide across the top where it clamps the bar, tapering to a rounded point at the bottom where it sits against the head tube/fork crown. Individual foam mounting blocks (image 1) are teardrop-shaped pucks under the main panel.

closure.hardware: RockLockster acrylic quick-release buckles standard (Austere machined buckles optional upgrade per source text)

details.fabric: X-Pac exterior over closed-cell foam, EPDM interior grip panel - see brand_notes.fabric
details.notes: Includes an 'Eye Patch' head-tube protector and 3D-printed H-Bar spacers per source text, neither clearly visible in these two photos.

mount.notes: Sits on top of and just forward of the bar, directly ahead of the stem, dropping down to rest against the head tube/fork crown area. On-bike photo confirms it works on drop bars (shown mounted between STI-style levers on a Chumba gravel bike) as well as flat bars per the maker's own description. No bag volume to render - a companion roll-top drybag (not sold by JPaks as part of this listing) would sit inside the cradle.
